survey: A short wooden pier running from a sandy beach out into shallow sea, seen at three-quarter view from the shore end. Posts: the front-left post is planted in the sand at the waterline, and the front-right post and two far posts stand in the water. Under the deck, a mid post stands in the water below the near span. Deck: plank boards run across two side stringers. The near end beam is bolted to the front-left post, and diagonal knee braces run from the front-left and front-right posts up to the underside of the deck. The far end of the deck rests between the two far posts. Rope: a thick rope is wound three times around the front-left post above deck level. It is a closed coil with no free end hanging in the air. Lifebuoy: a red-and-white ring hangs from a short rope loop over a peg on the front-right post, so it has a real attachment. The pier starts on the shore and ends in open water, as a pier should. Every load-bearing part rests on a post or a brace.
